timestamp_ns.description: Event timestamp in nanoseconds since Unix epoch

platform.description: Operating system that produced the event. Optional on the wire: an agent predating the platform-aware contract omits it and the server normalizes an absent value to darwin.

payload.description: Event body. The top-level "allOf" block selects which definition applies, keyed on "event_type".

signed.description: True when the package's signature chains to a certificate macOS trusts.

notarized.description: True when Apple's notary service accepted the package. Context, not trust.

team_id.description: The Developer ID team that signed the package, or empty when unsigned, untrusted, or signed by Apple itself.

item_type.description: BTM launch-item type (es_btm_item_type_t). 'daemon' = system-domain LaunchDaemon (T1543.004), 'agent' = LaunchAgent, 'login_item' = login item. 'unknown' is the extension's fallback for a future es_btm_item_type_t case it does not yet map.

item_path.description: The launch item as a file:// URL, as es_btm_launch_item_t.item_url reports it: the plist for a launch agent or daemon (for example file:///Library/LaunchAgents/com.example.plist), the app bundle for a login item or an app. An SMAppService item is reported relative to its app (app_url), and the agent resolves it against app_url before upload. A consumer matching or displaying it as a path must convert it; a path spells a space where the URL escapes it as %20.

app_url.description: Optional. The registering app's bundle as a file:// URL (es_btm_launch_item_t.app_url), present for an SMAppService item, which BTM names relative to it.

executable_path.description: Optional. POSIX executable path from the launchd plist, when available.

executable_code_signing.description: Optional. Code-signing of the registered executable (executable_path, or for a login item or an app, which have none, the app bundle item_path names), evaluated via SecStaticCode by the agent (the extension's sandbox cannot read the registered executable on a SIP-enabled host, so the agent fills this field before upload). This is the rule's decision input (the instigator is Apple's smd for launchctl-bootstrap registrations and cannot discriminate).

legacy.description: True iff a legacy plist-based launch item rather than an SMAppService registration.

managed.description: True iff managed by MDM. Managed daemons are operator-deployed and skipped by detection rules.

uid.description: User ID the item is registered for.

instigator_pid.description: Optional. PID of the process that registered the item (es_event_btm_launch_item_add_t.instigator). Forensic context only: for a launchctl-bootstrap registration the instigator is Apple's smd.

agent_session_env_value.description: An agent session marker's value. The extension drops a value longer than 256 UTF-8 bytes rather than truncate it. maxLength counts characters, so it is the looser bound a schema can express; the byte cap is the extension's.

cwd.description: Working directory at exec. Empty on startup snapshot rows, which cannot read it.

pidversion.description: Optional. Kernel PID generation (audit_token_to_pidversion) of the exec'd process, read from its audit token. Lets the server correlate flows to the exact process generation independently of PID reuse. Absent on agents that predate this field.

original_ppid.description: Optional. Parent pid at process creation. Unchanged when the process is reparented, so a double-forked daemon whose ppid is 1 (launchd) still names its creator. A pid only: the creator's generation is the fork event's parent_pidversion.

parent_pidversion.description: Optional. Kernel PID generation of the parent that ppid names (the current parent, launchd for a daemonized process), so ppid identifies one exact process.

responsible_pid.description: Optional. The process macOS holds responsible for this one. For a launchd-spawned XPC service, the app that requested it. For any process started from a terminal, the terminal app.

responsible_pidversion.description: Optional. Kernel PID generation of responsible_pid.

session_id.description: Optional. POSIX session id (the session leader's pid).

group_id.description: Optional. POSIX process group id. Survives daemonizing by double fork, nohup, or disown; replaced by setsid.

tty.description: Optional. Controlling terminal device path. Absent when the process has no controlling terminal.

start_time_ns.description: Optional. When the process was created (its fork), in Unix nanoseconds. Unchanged by exec. Startup snapshot rows carry it from the process table.

launchd_jobs.description: Optional. On a launchctl load or bootstrap exec, the job definitions of the plists it names, and of the .plist files directly in a directory it names, read by the agent from each plist the user who ran launchctl could read. Absent for any other exec, and when no named plist could be read.

plist_path.description: The plist, resolved against the exec's working directory when relative.

truncated.description: A field was cut to the bounds above.

env.description: Optional. AI agent session markers from the process's environment. Only the variables listed here are ever sent, matched on the full name: the rest of the environment holds credentials and never leaves the host. CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID equals the name of the Claude Code session's transcript file. Absent when the process carries no marker.

create_time_ns.description: Optional. Windows process creation time in Unix nanoseconds (from the kernel FILETIME). The platform-neutral pid_epoch (ADR-0018): the Windows analogue of macOS pidversion, disambiguating PID reuse. Absent on macOS events (which carry pidversion instead).

cdhash.description: Code-directory hash (sha1 of the CDDirectory blob) the agent extracts on Hardened-Runtime binaries (issue #68). Optional: NULL for non-HR processes since the ESF target tuple lacks a meaningful cdhash for them. 40 lowercase hex characters when present.

package_signing.description: Optional. On an installer script's exec only: the signature of the package the script belongs to, read by the agent from the package path PackageKit passes as the script's first argument. Set only when the exec's parent is Apple's package_script_service; absent when the package could not be read.

snapshot.description: True for synthetic exec events emitted at extension startup to materialise processes that existed before ESF subscription (issue #11). Detection rules skip snapshot events because they describe historical state, not new attacker activity.

pidversion.description: Optional. Kernel PID generation (audit_token_to_pidversion) of the CHILD process, read from its audit token. Stored on the new process generation so flows can correlate by exact identity. Absent on agents that predate this field.

parent_pidversion.description: Optional. Kernel PID generation of the forking process. With parent_pid it names the child's creator exactly, and it does not change when the child is later reparented.

pidversion.description: Optional. Kernel PID generation of the exiting process: the value its most recent exec event carried (its fork event, if it never exec'd), so the event joins the exact process row under pid reuse.

exit_reason.description: Optional. 'host_reconciled' tags exits synthesized by the agent's kill(pid,0) reconciliation pass when the kernel-observed exit event went missing (issue #6 client half). Absent or 'event' means the kernel observed the exit.

create_time_ns.description: Optional. Windows process creation time in Unix nanoseconds (the pid_epoch, ADR-0018), so an exit can be paired with the exec of the same (pid, create-time) generation. Absent on macOS events.

pidversion.description: Optional. Kernel PID generation of the acting process: the value its most recent exec event carried (its fork event, if it never exec'd), so the event joins the exact process row under pid reuse.
Optional. Kernel PID generation of the acting process: the value its most recent exec event carried (its fork event, if it never exec'd), so the event joins the exact process row under pid reuse.

source_path.description: Absolute path the file was renamed FROM. Required: a rename is the only watched operation that can make a file become sudo policy without any write to the destination, and the source is what distinguishes a promotion from a scratch path elsewhere from a move within the watched directory.

path.description: Absolute path the file was renamed TO. Named `path` rather than `destination_path` so it lines up with every other file event's target field, which is what the detection layer reads as TargetFilename.

pidversion.description: Optional. Kernel PID generation of the acting process: the value its most recent exec event carried (its fork event, if it never exec'd), so the event joins the exact process row under pid reuse.

path.description: Absolute path whose contents were discarded. Emitted for truncate(2)/ftruncate(2) and for an open(2) carrying O_TRUNC, which are different kernel paths reaching the same outcome: the file still exists and its contents are gone.

pidversion.description: Optional. Kernel PID generation of the acting process: the value its most recent exec event carried (its fork event, if it never exec'd), so the event joins the exact process row under pid reuse.

agent_credential_would_block_payload.description: An AI agent's process opened a credential file that is not its tool's, and the credential guard, in detect mode, let the open through. Only opens of the guarded files reach the guard, and only an agent's process that is not one of the credential's owner tools (matched by signing identity) is reported, so ssh reading a key for git push is not.

pidversion.description: Kernel PID generation of the opening process, which joins the event to its exec row and so to its path, signing and agent session.

path.description: Absolute path of the credential file opened.

credential.description: What the file holds: an SSH private key under ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.aws/credentials, the GitHub CLI's ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, ~/.netrc, ~/.docker/config.json or ~/.kube/config.

flags.description: The open's access mode as open(2) spells it: 0 O_RDONLY, 1 O_WRONLY, 2 O_RDWR.

agent_credential_block_payload.description: An AI agent's process opened a credential file that is not its tool's, and the credential guard, in protect mode, refused the open. The same shape as agent_credential_would_block.

file_activity_payload.description: File operations by one process in an AI agent's subtree, folded over a one-second window by the extension. Only processes an agent started are observed, so the event never describes the rest of the host. A type of its own rather than another open or file_rename, because those feed detection rules that read path as a file, and a rolled-up row names a directory.

pidversion.description: Kernel PID generation of the acting process, so the event joins the exact process row under pid reuse.

operation.description: What the process did: created a file or directory, closed a file it had changed, renamed one to path, removed one, or connected to the Unix-domain socket at path, the request to the daemon that serves it.

path.description: Absolute path operated on, or when rolled_up is true, the directory whose contents the counts cover.

source_path.description: Optional. Where the renamed file came from, shared by every rename the event folds. Absent for other operations, for an event folding renames from different sources, and for a rolled-up rename.

coalesced_count.description: Optional. How many operations the event stands for. Absent or 1 means one. The envelope timestamp_ns is the earliest.

last_timestamp_ns.description: Optional. Timestamp (ns since Unix epoch) of the latest operation the event stands for. Present only when coalesced_count is greater than 1.

rolled_up.description: Optional. True when the window held more rows than the extension sends a second, and path is a directory folding the operations on the paths under it.

agent_tool_call_payload.description: One tool call an AI agent recorded in its session transcript, read by the agent from the transcript on disk. The envelope timestamp_ns is the time the transcript gives the call. Only tool-call metadata is carried: never model output or tool results.

agent_session_id.description: The agent's own session id, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID for Claude Code, which the exec events of the session's processes also carry.

tool_use_id.description: The agent's id for the call, unique within the session.

tool_name.description: The tool called, e.g. Bash, Edit, Write or Read.

command.description: Optional. A Bash call's command, at most 8 KiB.

description.description: Optional. The description the agent gave a Bash call.

file_path.description: Optional. The path a file tool acted on.

cwd.description: Optional. The session's working directory when the call was made.

origin_session_id.description: Optional. The session id the transcript line was written under, where it differs from agent_session_id. A forked session's copy of its parent's history keeps the parent's id, so a call that the named session also holds is a copy of it.

forked_from_session_id.description: Optional. The session the call's session was forked from, as Claude Code's /fork job for the session names it (2.1.301 and later): direct evidence of the immediate parent.

prompt_id.description: Optional. The turn the call was made in, which the agent_prompt that began it also names.

sidechain.description: Optional. True when a subagent made the call inside the session.

truncated.description: Optional. True when command was cut to its 8 KiB limit.

uid.description: The uid of the transcript's owner, the user the call was read for. A transcript is its user's to write, so a call is trusted only for its owner's sessions.

agent_usage_payload.description: The tokens one assistant message of an AI agent session used, read by the agent from the session transcript on disk. One event per message however many transcript entries carry it, so the event_id is the same for each. The envelope timestamp_ns is the message's time in the transcript. Metadata only: no prompt or model text.

agent_session_id.description: The agent's own session id, as on agent_tool_call.

message_id.description: The message's id, as the model provider issued it.

model.description: The model that wrote the message.

input_tokens.description: Input tokens not read from the prompt cache.

cache_creation_input_tokens.description: Input tokens written to the prompt cache.

cache_read_input_tokens.description: Input tokens read from the prompt cache.

thinking_tokens.description: The part of output_tokens spent thinking.

prompt_id.description: Optional. The turn the message was made in, as on agent_tool_call.

permission_mode.description: Optional. The permission mode the transcript last put in force, as the agent records it (such as auto, acceptEdits, plan or bypassPermissions).

sidechain.description: Optional. True for a message a subagent wrote.

origin_session_id.description: Optional. The session the line names as its own where it differs from agent_session_id, as on agent_tool_call: a copy from it, or a message of a session /clear started.

forked_from_session_id.description: Optional. The session this one was forked from, as its /fork job names it, as on agent_tool_call.

uid.description: The uid of the transcript's owner, as on agent_tool_call.

agent_prompt_payload.description: One prompt a person gave an AI agent, typed or passed on the command line with claude -p, read by the agent from the session transcript on disk unless prompt capture is off. The envelope timestamp_ns is the time the transcript gives the prompt. Known secrets are redacted and the text is cut to 16 KiB before it is sent.

agent_session_id.description: The agent's own session id, as on agent_tool_call.

prompt_id.description: The turn the prompt began; the agent_tool_call events of the turn carry the same id.

text.description: What the person typed or passed, each recognized credential replaced by [REDACTED:<kind>], at most 16 KiB. A slash command reads as /name args.

length.description: The prompt's length in bytes as given, before redaction and the cut.

truncated.description: Optional. True when text was cut to its 16 KiB limit.

redacted.description: Optional. How many credentials were replaced in text.

source.description: Optional. How the prompt was entered, as the agent records it: typed, queued while the agent worked, a suggestion accepted, or sdk for one passed on the command line with claude -p.

cwd.description: Optional. The session's working directory when the prompt was sent.

uid.description: The uid of the transcript's owner, as on agent_tool_call.

pidversion.description: Optional. Kernel PID generation (audit_token_to_pidversion) of the source process, read from the flow's audit token. Lets the server correlate the flow to the exact process generation independently of PID reuse. Absent on agents that predate this field or when the flow carried no usable audit token.

coalesced_count.description: Optional. Number of occurrences this representative event stands for after agent-side coalescing (issue #408). The agent collapses repeated identical 5-tuples (pid, pidversion, protocol, direction, remote_address, remote_port) seen within the agent's coalescing window into one event. Absent or 1 means a single occurrence. The envelope timestamp_ns is the earliest occurrence.

last_timestamp_ns.description: Optional. Timestamp (ns since Unix epoch) of the latest occurrence in a coalesced series; the envelope timestamp_ns is the earliest. Present only when coalesced_count is greater than 1. Lets a consumer recover the span of the coalesced window.

response_addresses.description: Resolved addresses. After agent-side coalescing (issue #408) this is the union of every address observed across the merged queries for the same (pid, pidversion, query_name, query_type) within the agent's coalescing window, so a later connection to any resolved address still correlates.

pidversion.description: Optional. Kernel PID generation (audit_token_to_pidversion) of the querying process, read from the flow's audit token. Lets the server correlate the query to the exact process generation independently of PID reuse. Absent on agents that predate this field or when the flow carried no usable audit token.

coalesced_count.description: Optional. Number of occurrences this representative event stands for after agent-side coalescing (issue #408). The agent collapses repeated lookups for the same (pid, pidversion, query_name, query_type) seen within the agent's coalescing window into one event, merging a query with its follow-on response. Absent or 1 means a single occurrence. The envelope timestamp_ns is the earliest occurrence.

last_timestamp_ns.description: Optional. Timestamp (ns since Unix epoch) of the latest occurrence in a coalesced series; the envelope timestamp_ns is the earliest. Present only when coalesced_count is greater than 1.

snapshot_heartbeat_payload.description: Periodic liveness signal emitted by the agent for PIDs that were materialised via the issue #11 ESF startup snapshot. The server's graph builder updates processes.last_seen_ns on receipt; the TTL reconciler reads COALESCE(last_seen_ns, fork_time_ns) so a snapshot row with fresh heartbeats is exempt from the 6h force-exit (issue #173).

sensor_provider_transition_payload.description: A capture provider of the macOS network extension started or stopped (issues #649, #684). Emitted so a provider being switched off leaves a durable record on the server: agent health is level state, so once the self-heal (issue #632) restores the provider the health view reads healthy again and the fact that anything happened is gone. Disabling security tooling is MITRE T1562.001, so this is evidence an analyst works from rather than a diagnostic. Recovery is carried by the SUBSEQUENT running transition rather than by an outcome field: whether a stop was repaired is not known when the stop happens, and a pair of events (stopped at T, running at T+36s) states it without the emitter having to know anything about remediation.

provider.description: Capture provider wire identifier, e.g. content_filter or dns_proxy. Matches the extension's ProviderLiveness raw values.

state.description: State the provider transitioned INTO. Which stops appear here is decided by the extension's grading (issue #649): a stop it treats as deliberate absence is omitted from the report entirely and produces no transition, while a stop it treats as a fault appears as stopped. That grading is per provider, so switching off the OPTIONAL dns_proxy is absence and produces nothing, whereas switching off the mandatory content_filter is a fault and produces a stopped transition. The second case is the tamper-relevant one and is precisely what this event exists to record.

stop_reason.description: Raw NEProviderStopReason from the platform, carried unreduced so a consumer discriminates for itself rather than trusting a pre-collapsed verdict. Omitted for a running transition. Operator-driven values (userInitiated 1, providerDisabled 5, configurationDisabled 9) are the tamper-relevant ones; session-lifecycle values (configurationRemoved 10, superceded 11, userLogout 12, userSwitch 13) are what an ordinary upgrade or logout produces.

sensor_recovery_failed_payload.description: The agent's automatic repair of a stopped capture provider ran out of attempts and a human is now required (issues #632, #691). This is a separate event from sensor_provider_transition rather than a field on it, because it reports the outcome of REMEDIATION, not a change of provider state: the provider is still stopped, and no transition has occurred. It exists because the transition pair alone cannot express it. A stop with no following running transition means either 'still trying' or 'gave up', and those carry opposite urgency for an analyst; only the agent knows which, and only at the moment its budget is spent. Emitted exactly once per stop episode, at the edge where the budget is exhausted, NOT on every liveness report while the provider stays down.

provider.description: Capture provider wire identifier, e.g. content_filter or dns_proxy. Matches the extension's ProviderLiveness raw values. Bounded because the server stores it as an identifying column on the health record it opens, and a value that does not fit would fail that write and stall the batch behind it; a longer value is refused rather than recorded.

outcome.description: Which failure shape was reached, because they point a responder at different things. Known values: enable_failed, meaning the repair command itself kept failing, which implicates the host app or the configuration daemon; and enable_ineffective, meaning every repair reported SUCCESS and the provider stayed stopped anyway, which means re-enabling is simply not what this fault needs. Both leave the host not capturing. Deliberately NOT an enum: a newer agent reporting a shape an older server has no phrasing for must still raise the finding, described in general terms, rather than being rejected at the boundary or silently dropped. The server's handling of an unrecognised value is a stated requirement, and an enum here would contradict it.

attempts.description: How many repair attempts were made before giving up. At least 1: the event is only emitted once the budget is spent, which cannot happen without an attempt. Bounded above by the agent's attempt budget; carried so an analyst can see the repair was genuinely tried rather than skipped.

component.description: The registered health component that OWNS the provider, e.g. network_extension. Carried because the fault is recorded against a component and closed when that component reports healthy again, and the provider alone cannot name one: a provider is rendered into the health snapshot from its parent's liveness report and vanishes the moment the parent stops reporting it, so a later snapshot has nothing to match it against. The agent knows its parent at the moment it gives up, so it says so, rather than leaving the server to keep a provider-to-component map that would rot silently the first time a provider moved. Optional: an agent predating this field omits it, and the server records the fault without one rather than dropping the report.

rule_id.description: Stable string identifier of the matched application-control rule (e.g. "app_control:42"). Echoed by the server as the alert's rule_id.

identifier.description: The matched identifier value (e.g. the SHA-256 the BINARY rule matched against).

application_control_would_block_payload.description: Emitted when AUTH_EXEC matched a BLOCK rule whose enforcement is DETECT and the policy allowed the exec, so it ran. The shape is the application_control_block payload's: identifier is the value that matched the DETECT rule.

application_control_undecided_payload.description: Emitted when AUTH_EXEC could not compute a BINARY hash within the kernel deadline budget (or the file was unreadable for the TOCTOU re-stat reasons in FileHashCache.computeSHA256WithDeadline) and the active snapshot's deadline_fallback drove the verdict. Operators consume these events to size their cold-cache rate before flipping the posture between fail-closed / fail-open / audit-only.

verdict.description: Wire verdict the kernel received. "deny" only fires under fail-closed posture; "allow" fires under audit-only (fail-open emits no event by design).

reason.description: Technical cause that prevented a hash decision. "deadline" means the budget headroom was exhausted before chunks finished streaming; "read_failed" means the file could not be opened, fstat failed, or a TOCTOU replace was detected between AUTH and read.

file_size_bytes.description: Size of the executable being authorised. Pairs with reason="deadline" to identify large-binary workloads where the deadline budget is the bottleneck.

application_control_resync_payload.description: Emitted when the extension accepts an application-control snapshot whose policy_version regressed below the active snapshot's but whose policy_epoch (the policy's server-assigned updated_at in microseconds) advanced. That pairing is the signature of a server database restore-from-backup or reset: policy_version restarts low while the host retains a higher persisted version, so the version-only gate would freeze enforcement. The extension re-syncs on the epoch axis and emits this event so the regression is operator-visible instead of being a host-only log line (#322).

previous_version.description: The policy_version the host held before accepting the regressed snapshot.

new_version.description: The lower policy_version the host re-synced to.

previous_epoch.description: The policy_epoch (updated_at microseconds) the host held before the re-sync.

new_epoch.description: The advanced policy_epoch that drove acceptance despite the version regression.

reason.description: Why the re-sync fired. "version_regression" is the only cause today: a lower version accepted because the epoch advanced.

service.description: The TCC service whose permission changed, as tccd names it without the kTCCService prefix (for example SystemPolicyAllFiles for Full Disk Access, Accessibility, ScreenCapture, ListenEvent for Input Monitoring).

identity.description: The app the permission is about, as identity_type says: a bundle identifier or an executable path, usually.

update_type.description: Whether the permission record was created, modified or deleted.

right.description: The permission the record holds after the change.

reason.description: Why the record changed: user_consent is a prompt answered, user_set a switch changed in System Settings, mdm_policy a configuration profile.

instigator_pid.description: The process that made the change (tccd's client).

responsible_pid.description: Optional. The process responsible for the change, when macOS reports one.

identity_path.description: Optional. The app's path, added by the agent: the identity itself when it is an executable path, or the application LaunchServices has for it when it is a bundle identifier.

identity_code_signing.description: Optional. The app's on-disk code signing, read by the agent from identity_path. Whether a permission went to Apple's software or to something else is judged from this.
